title: 2D Adaptive: only the first region gets the helix entry; each other entry is a straight plunge into material, with no warning

labels.name: claimed
labels.description: An agent is working on this - see the claim comment

labels.name: P1
labels.description: Unsafe or wrong output: gouge, collision, wrong G-code, crash, data loss; blocks a cut

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
Reported by the maintainer in chat, 2026-11-16, with two screenshots (build `v0.22.0 · f6c7f605`, a local test build):

> "Bug in 2D Adapive. This was generated by setting a stock boundary and picking the outside edge of the part. I will helix down the first hole and clearing it out all the other Entrys inside and outside the part is missing lead ins of same helix setting. Same issue if i remove the boundary.. Only a helix leadin on the first pocket.. not the secondd one. This kinda comes back to how containment is getting interpreted... But problem ppeprsista even if i pick two inside faces of the pockets.. Helix is only on the first pocket, second is justa straight plunge into the material with no warning."

What happens:

- Project `testdata/models/fig8.camproj` (model `fig8.step`), 2D Adaptive, tool `EM-0800-4FL` (8 mm end mill), post Fanuc (built-in).
- Lead in / Lead out page: Entry Type `Helix`, Helix radius 1.6 mm, Minimum radius, pitch and angle on Auto, Plunge enabled.
- The operation generates: "8832 moves (27 plunge(s) @ 300, 3 level(s), 2286 arc(s)), 12 warning(s)".
- The first pocket gets the helix entry. Each other entry, inside and outside the part, is a straight plunge into the material.
- No warning names the plunges.
- The result is the same for three selections: stock boundary with the outside edge; no boundary; the two inside faces of the pockets.

Expected:

- Each entry into material uses the selected entry type (helix), at each region and each level.
- Where the helix does not fit, the ramp comes next. A straight plunge into material is the last fallback only.
- Each entry that falls back gets a warning that names the region, the level and the reason. The page says "where the helix cannot fit, a ramp and then a plunge stand in": the user must see when this happens.
- A plunge into material with a tool that cannot cut at its centre is refused or blocks the post, by the rule that the project has for such tools.
- A plunge in open air (outside the stock, or in an area that an earlier pass cleared) needs no helix and no warning.

To find:

1. Why the entry planner gives the helix to the first region only. Does it try the helix for each region, or one time for the operation?
2. If the 27 plunges are in material or in cleared area, by the stock state at that moment.
3. If the Offset rings fallback is the cause. The status line says "the HSM plan is refused: the area is a channel 10.6 mm wide ..."; the fallback path possibly does not apply the entry settings.
4. Why no warning is made.

Safety: a straight plunge into uncut material without a warning is wrong output that can break a tool. The fix changes posted G-code of 2D Adaptive (entry moves) and is under the safety floor. The verify check and the post gate do not become weaker. No real control run exists.

Related: #2232 (containment Outside, option 1 selected), and the "feed moves cross in XY at shared depth" warnings on this project (seen in the review of PR #2214).

Done means: a test on a part with two separate pockets (and one with an outside region) asserts a helix or ramp entry at each region and level where it fits, and a named warning for each entry that falls back to a plunge in material. The goldens that change are named in the PR.
